newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr maintains firm tone versus yen in late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dlr maintains firm tone versus yen in late Tokyo.

text.p: 0625 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar maintained a firm tone against the yen by late afternoon Tokyo trade on Tuesday but remained within a relatively narrow range due to a lack of fresh news.
Earlier, the dollar briefly slipped below 118 yen, but it drifted back up on comments by senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara.
Sakakibara, Japan's vice finance minister for international affairs, told Reuters on Tuesday that he makes no comments on exchange rates or any rumours in the currency markets.
Talk has circulated in the market since late last week that the Finance Ministry warned currency traders not to buy dollars above 119 yen.
"I do not have any comments on foreign exchange moves. I do not make any comments on any rumours in the forex market," Sakakibara said.
"The dollar was lifted by Sakakibara's remarks but its upside was heavy around 118.50 yen," said a city bank trader.
In addition to short-covering by interbank players, some Japanese importers bought dollars after Sakakibara's remarks, traders said.
Mark buying against the yen by U.S. investment banks also helped to push the greenback higher versus the Japanese currency in early trade, traders said.
But the dollar's upside was capped by selling by Japanese institutional investors above 118.50 yen.
Some Japanese exporters lowered their dollar offers after seeing that the dollar's topside was heavy near 119 yen, a trader at a long-term credit bank said.
Despite the Finance Ministry's silence over recent currency movements, Tokyo operators were still cautious about possible verbal interventions.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka declined on Tuesday to comment on short-term movements in the currency market, saying that forex rates are decided by supply and demand conditions within the market.
"People are reluctant to push the dollar too high, as they doubt that the Finance Ministry will keep quiet when the dollar rises above 120 yen," said a trader at another city bank.
A trader at another city bank said some Japanese investors were still keen to buy dollars below 118 yen.

The dollar briefly rose above 1.87 marks in late Tokyo trade after the Bundesbank set a 14-day securities repurchase tender at a fixed rate of 3.0 percent while making no comments on any other money market activities.
There had been speculation that the Bundesbank might announce an additional tender at variable interest rates, which would have effectively allowed repo rates to rise.
Earlier, uncertainty about Buba moves had helped underpin the mark, traders said.
"Europeans sold marks as Buba did not announce a move to a variable repo rate today, but the dollar was capped by profit-taking above 1.87 marks," said a trader at a trust bank.

The Bundesbank surprised the market on July 24 by setting securities repurchase tenders at a fixed rate of three percent for the next two weeks only, leaving the market guessing about the repo rate in the second half of its four-week summer break.
The dollar closed at 118.28/38 yen and 1.8655/65 marks in New York on Monday.
-- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
